name: N-PAMP handshake + keyed-session state machine (per endpoint)
model: Mealy machine of RECEIVER reactions: (role, state, received-frame) -> (output, next_state). Output is the endpoint's observable reaction (a sent frame, an ERROR with its wire code, or SILENT). This is the reference model the T18.1 deviant-trace generator and the T18.2 learned-model diff both compare against.

provenance.authority_note: DERIVED FROM THE DRAFT TEXT (the normative event-by-state rules and the total default), NOT from any implementation. This independence is required for F3 non-circularity: the T18.2 learned-model diff compares the Go stack's LEARNED machine against THIS table, so the table must not itself be derived from Go, or the comparison would be Go-vs-Go.

input_meaning.SERVER_HELLO_BADSEL: SERVER_HELLO carrying a selection the initiator did not offer (draft:836-837)
input_meaning.SERVER_AUTH_BADAUTH: SERVER_AUTH whose AEAD open, CertVerify signature, or Finished MAC fails (draft:856-858)
input_meaning.CLIENT_AUTH_BADAUTH: CLIENT_AUTH whose AEAD open, CertVerify signature, or Finished MAC fails (draft:856-858)
input_meaning.APP: an application frame on any channel
input_meaning.UNKNOWN: a frame of an unknown or unexpected type (draft:872-873)

output_meaning.SILENT: no frame emitted (internal state advance, a discard, or a terminal state); on the wire the endpoint sends nothing in reaction
output_meaning.SILENT_ABORT: the endpoint tears down WITHOUT sending an ERROR frame, because no traffic key is yet established (a pre-key state): sending an ERROR would be an unauthenticated frame an off-path attacker could forge. The peer detects the abort via the transport (connection close) or the handshake-completion timer (draft:452-459).
output_meaning.SH_SA: the responder sends SERVER_HELLO followed by the AEAD-sealed SERVER_AUTH (draft:848-849)
output_meaning.KEY_UPDATE_ACK: the endpoint sends KEY_UPDATE_ACK and stays ESTABLISHED (draft:863-864)
output_meaning.CLOSE_ACK: the endpoint seals and sends CLOSE_ACK (draft:864-866)
output_meaning.ACCEPT: an application frame is processed in place with no protocol-level reaction (draft:862)
output_meaning.ERROR:unexpected_message: a fatal ERROR frame carrying the registered code unexpected_message, then teardown (draft:870-878)
output_meaning.ERROR:decrypt_failed: a fatal ERROR frame carrying the registered code decrypt_failed, then teardown, deriving no session keys (draft:856-858)

unexpected_message.note: total default; asserted on the wire (draft:880-885)

decrypt_failed.note: AEAD/CertVerify/Finished failure at WAIT_SA or WAIT_CA (draft:856-858)

key_update_out_of_order.note: a KeyUpdateMarker (on KEY_UPDATE or KEY_UPDATE_ACK) that is malformed or announces an epoch != current+1 (draft error registry row 9, §key-update). A code-level refinement BELOW the abstract alphabet: the learner presents only well-formed markers, so this is covered by the deviant-trace suite (statetrace_test.go key_update_*_out_of_order), not learned coverage.

handshake_timeout.note: timer-fired, not an input symbol (APPROVAL row 13)

close_incomplete.note: CLOSE_ACK-wait timer expiry (draft:866-867); timer, not an input symbol

transitions.note: checks every selection was offered, derives handshake keys, advances (draft:836-839)

a selection not offered is rejected (draft:836-837); WAIT_SH is PRE-KEY (the initiator has not yet processed SERVER_HELLO to derive handshake keys), so the abort sends no ERROR frame (draft:452-459). The transcript binding additionally catches a downgraded-but-offered selection later at the Finished MAC.
verifies CertVerify + Finished, sends CLIENT_AUTH, derives master, ESTABLISHED once CLIENT_AUTH is sent (draft:840-844)
failed AEAD/CertVerify/Finished is a fatal handshake authentication failure, derive no keys (draft:856-858)
selects profile/algorithms, sends SERVER_HELLO + sealed SERVER_AUTH (draft:848-850)
verifies CertVerify + Finished; reaches ESTABLISHED with no ack frame (draft:851-854)
failed AEAD/CertVerify/Finished at WAIT_CA is fatal, derive no keys (draft:856-858)
application frames on any open channel processed in place (draft:862)
epoch advances, KEY_UPDATE_ACK sent, remains ESTABLISHED (draft:863-864)
receiving an authenticated CLOSE: process in-flight, seal+send CLOSE_ACK, terminate (draft:864-866; APPROVAL row 13 / D7)
the closer awaits CLOSE_ACK; on CLOSE_ACK it moves to CLOSED (draft:866-867)

draft:436-438 — the closer, in CLOSING while awaiting CLOSE_ACK, MAY continue to receive and process frames the peer had in flight; an in-flight application frame is processed in place (like ESTABLISHED), the endpoint stays CLOSING. Corrects the earlier over-derivation (modeled_exclusions) that routed all non-CLOSE_ACK CLOSING inputs through the total default.
draft:436-438 — an in-flight KEY_UPDATE received while CLOSING is processed like ESTABLISHED (epoch advance, KEY_UPDATE_ACK), the endpoint stays CLOSING.

draft:432-438 — simultaneous close: a verified CLOSE received while this endpoint is itself CLOSING is processed as any received CLOSE (in-flight drained, CLOSE_ACK sealed and sent), then teardown (CLOSED).

total_default.rule: In any NON-TERMINAL state, a received frame with no explicit transition above — a handshake frame out of order, a frame from a later or earlier flight, a repeated frame, an application frame before ESTABLISHED, or any unknown/unexpected type — is a fatal unexpected_message and the connection is torn down. An endpoint MUST NOT silently ignore an unexpected frame and MUST NOT recover by skipping it. The OBSERVABLE reaction depends on whether a traffic key is established (draft:448-459): in a POST-KEY state the endpoint MUST send a sealed ERROR frame (0x0005, Control channel 0x0000, AEAD-protected) carrying unexpected_message before teardown; in a PRE-KEY state it aborts WITHOUT an ERROR (no unauthenticated ERROR an off-path attacker could forge) and the peer detects the abort via the transport or the handshake-completion timer.
total_default.provenance: draft:870-878 (total default); draft:448-459 (pre-key silent abort vs post-key sealed ERROR)

exceptions.note: CLOSED is terminal; no frame is processed and there is no connection to tear down (draft:868). This is the one state where a non-listed input does not emit unexpected_message.

a replayed (previously-seen sequence number) frame is a DISCARD code (replay_detected), silently dropped with no ERROR, state unchanged (draft:884-886). Replay is a sequence-number property, modeled out of the abstract alphabet (see exclusions).

unauthenticated_inputs.provenance: draft:498 (error-registry row 2: in an ESTABLISHED keyed session an AEAD-open failure is NOT decrypt_failed — it is a silently-dropped, counted record whose association survives) + draft:903-908 (the record-layer drop rule {#record-layer-drops}); Part-3 (D16). Matches DTLS 1.3 RFC 9147 §4.5.2 and QUIC RFC 9001 §6.6.2.
unauthenticated_inputs.rule: These abstract inputs are concretized by the SUL as UNAUTHENTICATED frames once a keyed session with a live *Conn exists (ESTABLISHED/CLOSING): CLIENT_HELLO / SERVER_HELLO / SERVER_HELLO_BADSEL are sent CLEARTEXT (no FlagENC), and *_BADAUTH are sealed-then-corrupted so the AEAD open FAILS. Per the record-layer drop rule a cleartext or AEAD-failing frame at a keyed state is silently DROPPED and counted and the association SURVIVES — no output (SILENT), no state change (self-loop). This encodes the modeled_exclusions 'Unauthenticated input in ESTABLISHED' note as a machine-readable rule the T18.2 diff expansion honors (previously it fell through to the total-default ERROR, which the Part-3 drop-and-survive impl correctly does NOT do). SERVER_AUTH / CLIENT_AUTH (non-BADAUTH) are deliberately EXCLUDED here: the SUL seals them validly, so a validly-authenticated but wrong-flight frame in ESTABLISHED IS the total default (unexpected_message) — which is why sealed SERVER_AUTH stays ERROR and is the regression anchor proving the total default still fires. Applies only at states with a live *Conn / record-layer drop path (ESTABLISHED, CLOSING); at the pre-establishment handshake states the handshake driver, not recvLocked, governs, so this rule does not apply there.

modeled_exclusions: Sequence numbers / the replay window: outside a plain Mealy-machine model (R18.2 sanctions this); covered by targeted differential testing (T8.1 replay KAT), not learned coverage. replay_detected is a discard (SILENT).

Unauthenticated input in ESTABLISHED (a cleartext / not-AEAD-protected frame, or a frame whose AEAD tag fails to verify — a forged or corrupted sealed frame, or a frame at an out-of-sequence position): BELOW the abstract alphabet — it never authenticates, so it is not a receiver-reaction input symbol. Per the record-layer drop rule (draft {#record-layer-drops}) it is silently DROPPED and counted and the association SURVIVES (no output, no state change), matching DTLS 1.3 RFC 9147 §4.5.2 and QUIC RFC 9001 §6.6.2. This is precisely what lets the T18.2 SUL scope the learned model to AUTHENTICATED inputs: unauthenticated input produces no output and no state transition, so the learner cannot trip on session-death. Covered by the drop-and-survive tests (impl/go/sdk/dropsurvive_test.go + conn_guards_test.go's replay case), not by learned coverage. A frame that fails to PARSE at the wire level is instead a fatal transport error (the byte stream is untrustworthy), distinct from a survivable drop.

Timer-fired transitions: CLOSING->CLOSED on CLOSE_ACK-wait timeout (close_incomplete) and the handshake-completion timeout (handshake_timeout) are NOT input symbols (no frame arrives); covered by the T11.1 timeout test and the T12.1 timer bounds.

In-flight frames arriving at the CLOSING closer before CLOSE_ACK: draft:436-438 — the closer in CLOSING, while awaiting CLOSE_ACK, MAY continue to receive and process frames the peer had in flight. CLOSING is therefore modeled to MIRROR ESTABLISHED for received frames (APP->ACCEPT, KEY_UPDATE->KEY_UPDATE_ACK, CLOSE->CLOSE_ACK->CLOSED, unauthenticated->drop-survive SILENT via unauthenticated_inputs, sealed-unexpected->total-default), plus the CLOSING-only CLOSE_ACK->CLOSED transition. This CORRECTS an earlier over-derivation of this note, which wrongly routed every non-CLOSE_ACK CLOSING input through the total default (unexpected_message) — stricter than the draft's MAY-process rule and contradicted by the draft's own §CLOSE text. The distinction CLOSING keeps from ESTABLISHED (it has already SENT a CLOSE and is awaiting the ack) is not observable via received-frame reactions, so a learner correctly collapses CLOSING into ESTABLISHED; the reference now matches that.

START (initiator) is a transient send-first state: the initiator sends CLIENT_HELLO as its opening ACTION (not a reaction to a received frame) and advances to WAIT_SH. A SUL for the initiator resets into WAIT_SH (CLIENT_HELLO already sent). START is listed for completeness; any frame received in START is total-default unexpected_message (draft:834-835 'No frame is legal to receive in START').

Master-ratchet / re-KEM control frames in ESTABLISHED (MASTER_RATCHET 0x0104, MASTER_RATCHET_ACK 0x0105, REKEM 0x0106, REKEM_ACK 0x0107 on the Control channel): these are legal record-layer control frames in ESTABLISHED (draft ESTABLISHED bullet + total-default carve-out) belonging to a SEPARATE multi-generation sub-protocol (the Hybrid Tree Ratchet, spec/10 section 9). Modeling their generation-indexed state in a flat Mealy machine would explode the state space, so they are excluded from the learned abstract alphabet — the same treatment as sequence numbers and timers — and covered by the dedicated ratchet differential tests (impl/go/sdk/ratchet_test.go, ratchet_e2e_test.go), NOT by learned coverage. Consequently the T18.1 deviant generator MUST concretize the abstract UNKNOWN symbol to an unassigned reserved type (e.g. 0x00FE), never to 0x0104-0x0107, or a correct impl would answer a ratchet ACK where the table expects unexpected_message. KEY_UPDATE/KEY_UPDATE_ACK, by contrast, are a simple epoch bump the draft state machine DOES list, so they stay in the modeled alphabet.

KEY_UPDATE_ACK solicited path: the abstract KEY_UPDATE_ACK input models the UNSOLICITED acknowledgement (received with no matching KEY_UPDATE this endpoint sent) -> total default unexpected_message, which is what the learner presents (it never first drives the SUL to send a KEY_UPDATE and await the ack). The SOLICITED path (an initiator correlating the ack to its own outstanding KEY_UPDATE -> SILENT) is modeled OUT of this flat Mealy machine — it depends on send-side pending state (per (channel, epoch)) the learner does not drive, the same treatment as sequence numbers, timers, and the ratchet generation state. It is covered by the sdk correlation unit + e2e tests (pendingack_test.go, keyupdate_e2e_test.go), not by learned coverage. The same holds for MASTER_RATCHET_ACK / REKEM_ACK: an unsolicited one is unexpected_message, covered by statetrace_test.go + the ratchet differential tests. A malformed KeyUpdateMarker on either KEY_UPDATE or its ACK is key_update_out_of_order (wire_codes), also below the abstract alphabet.
